cohort: 160 nulliparous women with singleton term pregnancies, stratified into normal weight (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), and obese (>=30.0 kg/m2) BMI categories.
finding: Increasing maternal BMI in nulliparous women is associated with higher risks of labour induction, caesarean delivery, prolonged labour, neonatal macrosomia, and maternal wound infections.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal BMI in nulliparous women is associated with a significantly higher incidence of labour induction and caesarean delivery.
